newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam's first bourse feasible by 2000 - minister.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam's first bourse feasible by 2000 - minister.

text.p: Vietnam could have its first stock exchange up and running before the end of the century, new Finance Minister Nguyen Sinh Hung said on Monday.
Asked by reporters during a break in National Assembly proceedings if it was likely that a bourse would be established before 2000, he replied: "Yes, I think it is feasible."
Hung said that while it was necessary for Vietnam to have a stock market, a legal framework had to be worked out first and tradeable shares and bonds had to be issued.
"As you know the stock market is very sensitive and very complicated," he said. "In this respect I really think that state management is necessary, otherwise risks would increase."
Earlier this year, the ruling Communist Party listed the gradual establishment of a capital market and stock exchange among its goals, but gave no timetable.
Hanoi has been planning a stock market for some years, encouraged by the success of economic reforms along market lines.
But it has acknowledged the obstacles lying in its way.
So far, fewer than a dozen of the country's roughly 6,000 state-owned enterprises have been "equitised" -- Vietnam's term for the sale of minority stakes in companies in lieu of full privatisation.
Other hurdles yet to be cleared include the country's primitive accounting regulations and its still-nascent banking industry.
Hung said Vietnamese nationals and foreigners would be offered the chance of investing in the stock market.
Foreigners would be able to participate by subscribing to sovereign debt which Hanoi hopes to issue on the international market some time in the future.
